newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Sweden "well qualified" for EMU, PM says.
newsitem.headline: Sweden "well qualified" for EMU, PM says.

text.p: Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Saturday that Sweden would be well qualified to join the European Union's planned monetary union, but reiterated that any decision to apply would be made by the national parliament.

Persson told Reuters Financial Television said Sweden would meet the conditions for the single currency laid down by the Maastricht treaty and rejected any comparisons with countries such as Spain and Italy.
Asked about funds flowing into high-yielding currencies, Persson said: "I don't think you should compare Sweden with Spain and Italy...We stand alone."

Noting that Swedish bond yields are now below those in Britain, Persson said: "We have left that group, I must say. And we have such a strong performance in our public finances and we have almost zero inflation. So of course Sweden is very attractive (for investors)."
Persson said France and Germany would be "obvious" participants in economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start in 1999.
Asked whether Sweden may be in EMU fairly early on, he said: "Perhaps...we have the ability and we will reach the convergence criteria...so we will be well qualified to participate."
The Swedish parliament is due to decide in the autumn of 1997 on whether the country should apply to join EMU.
